title: Mechanized stamp milling
summary: Cam-lifted trip hammers crushed ore for further processing at Roman mining sites; surviving examples attest the machine in the first and second centuries CE.

parents.reason: Water wheels supplied the rotating shafts that lifted and dropped the mill's ore-crushing stamps.

title: Hydraulic placer mining
summary: High-pressure water jets dislodged gold-bearing gravel for sluice separation in California's first modern hydraulic mines.

title: Patio silver amalgamation
summary: Mercury and salt brine recovered silver from ground ores at scale; Medina is credited with adding copper-sulfate magistral, though its necessity is disputed.

title: Gold cyanidation
summary: The MacArthur–Forrest process dissolved gold from low-grade ores in cyanide solution, making previously refractory Rand ores workable.

title: Merrill zinc-dust gold recovery
summary: Merrill's circa-1900 process replaced zinc shavings with zinc dust to recover dissolved gold from cyanide leach solutions.

parents.reason: Cyanide leaching creates the gold-bearing solution; Merrill used zinc dust to precipitate its gold, replacing zinc shavings.

title: Industrial ball mill
summary: Rotating shells and loose grinding media produced fine powders; a reported 1870 use ground flint for pottery.

title: Industrial agitation froth flotation
summary: The Sulman–Picard–Ballot process used limited oil and agitation to create bubbles that carried sulfide minerals into a froth; it succeeded at Broken Hill in 1905.

title: Frasch sulfur extraction
summary: Concentric pipes injected superheated water and air to melt and lift elemental sulfur from deep underground deposits.

title: Commercial copper electrorefining
summary: Commercial electrolytic refining deposited high-purity copper from impure anodes in the first successful plant at Pembrey, Wales.

title: Mechanized carding machine
summary: Lewis Paul's patented hand-driven machines used wire-covered surfaces to separate and align fibers before spinning; mill use expanded in the 1780s.

title: Mechanized wool-combing machine
summary: Cartwright's patented machine laid wool fibers parallel by length before further treatment, mechanizing a distinct worsted-yarn preparation stage.

title: Roller printing on textiles
summary: Thomas Bell's patented cylinder process transferred engraved patterns onto fabric continuously, reducing the cost of copperplate textile printing.

title: Ring spinning frame
summary: The ring frame continuously drew, twisted, and wound yarn; John Thorp's Rhode Island design is credited to 1828 or 1829.

parents.reason: The ring frame descended from the water frame's powered roller drafting and spindle-based twisting arrangement.

title: Mercerization of cotton
summary: John Mercer's caustic-soda treatment strengthened cotton and increased its affinity for dyes; tension-induced luster was a later refinement.

parents.reason: Mercer's finishing treatment acts directly on woven cotton fabric to improve strength and dye uptake.

title: Mauveine synthetic dye
summary: Perkin’s accidental oxidation of aniline impurities produced mauveine, one of the earliest synthetic textile dyes to be mass-produced.

title: Synthetic alizarin dye
summary: Graebe and Liebermann developed a synthetic route from anthracene to the red madder dye, undercutting cultivation of the natural source.

title: Pfleger synthetic indigo process
summary: Pfleger’s 1901 route used an alkaline melt of N-phenylglycine to form indoxyl, which was then oxidized in air to produce indigo.

title: Nitroglycerin explosive
summary: Sobrero's nitration of glycerol produced a powerful but shock-sensitive liquid explosive later used in blasting and mining.

title: Dynamite
summary: Nobel stabilized nitroglycerin in an absorbent material and patented a more manageable explosive for construction, demolition, and mining.

parents.reason: Dynamite's explosive charge is nitroglycerin made safer to handle by absorption into a porous material.

title: Wire rope for mine hoists
summary: Albert's multi-strand iron-wire ropes replaced weaker hemp ropes and failure-prone chains in Harz mining hoists.

parents.reason: Wire drawing supplies the long metal filaments twisted together to form a load-bearing rope.

title: Davy safety lamp
summary: A flame-surrounding wire gauze prevented a lamp from igniting methane in coal mines; Davy presented his design in November 1815.

parents.reason: Fine drawn wire made the gauze screen that confined the lamp flame while admitting air.

title: Industrial steam hammer
summary: The first working steam hammer delivered controlled heavy blows for shaping large iron and steel forgings.

parents.reason: Forging supplied the metal-shaping operation that the steam-powered ram enlarged for heavy workpieces.
parents.directContribution: Forging is the work the hammer performs: its steam-driven ram deforms hot metal, independently of the steam engine that supplies power.

parents.reason: The boiler supplied the working steam admitted to the machine cylinder and directly drove its powered motion.
parents.directContribution: The boiler directly supplied working steam to the hammer cylinder; the atmospheric pumping engine is a separate power-machine milestone.

title: Steam-powered rock drill
summary: Trevithick's steam drill mechanized boring into rock and was used chiefly in surface quarries where boilers could be brought nearby.

parents.reason: The boiler supplied the working steam admitted to the machine cylinder and directly drove its powered motion.
